narrator.instruct: Gripping, energetic storyteller telling a dramatic true history what-if, brisk, punchy and excited, never calm.

gerard.instruct: A young army general bursting into a room, urgent and pleading, almost shouting at his commander.

grouchy.instruct: A stiff, stubborn army marshal refusing an argument, firm, cold and final.

blucher.instruct: A fierce old cavalry general on horseback roaring at his troops, gruff and fired up.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Napoleon's best chance at Waterloo may have been sitting at breakfast, eating strawberries.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Belgium, June eighteenth, eighteen fifteen. Napoleon, back from exile, has a new army. In front of him, Wellington. Somewhere east, the Prussians, beaten two days earlier.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A day earlier, Napoleon sent Marshal Grouchy and over thirty thousand men after the Prussians, to keep them away.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: It rains all night. Napoleon waits for the mud to dry, giving the Prussians time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Miles away, Grouchy is at breakfast. Strawberries, the story goes. Then a low rumble, from the west. Cannons.

lines.speaker: gerard
lines.text: Marshal, we must march to the guns!

lines.speaker: grouchy
lines.text: My orders are to follow the Prussians.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So he keeps chasing, into a rear guard at Wavre. Most Prussians have already slipped away toward Waterloo.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: By late afternoon, they crash into Napoleon's side.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: His last attack breaks. His army runs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Wellington called it the nearest run thing you ever saw.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Now, what if Grouchy had turned around? Some historians say he'd have arrived too late anyway.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Even winning that day probably wouldn't have saved Napoleon. Austrian and Russian armies were already marching on France.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Most historians think he'd still have lost, just somewhere else.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the strawberries probably didn't change the war. Just which village gave us "meet your Waterloo."
